intended_object: The map in Stone duality for spectral spaces that sends a prime ideal P of the lattice of compact opens of a spectral space X to a point of X: the generic point of the irreducible closed set ⋂_{U∈P} Uᶜ. It is the inverse of x ↦ {U | x ∉ U}. This comes from the docstring, the module documentation and how the library uses it.
explanation:
The body takes the generic point, which exists because X is sober, of `primeClosedSet X P = ⋂_{U ∈ P} Uᶜ`. The library proves that this set is closed, nonempty and irreducible. Nonemptiness uses that ⊤ is compact and not in P, and irreducibility uses that P is prime and the compact opens form a basis.

This is the standard construction from the literature (e.g. Fujiwara–Kato, 0.2.2.8; Hochster/Stone duality). The library also proves `spaceToSpectrum (spectrumToSpace P) = P`, which confirms that it is the intended inverse.

The setting fits the construction. Sobriety is needed for the generic point, and compactness of X is needed for ⊤ to be a compact open, so that P is proper and the closed set is nonempty. Spectral spaces are therefore the natural generality. `PrimeIdealSpectrum` is the library's own type: the prime order ideals of a bounded distributive lattice. Mathlib has no counterpart for this Stone-duality map.
